159516038.title: File:Rockefeller Memorial Chapel, University of Chicago, 59th Street and Woodlawn Avenue, Hyde Park, Chicago, IL.jpg

ImageDescription.value: Designed in 1918-1924 and built in 1925-1928, this Gothic Revival-style chapel was designed by Bertram Goodhue and Hildreth Meière to serve as a chapel for the University of Chicago, utilizing funds donated by John D. Rockefeller to the school for the construction of a chapel, which was intended to be a dominant feature of the campus.  The building is clad in limestone with large gothic arched bays housing stained glass windows and tracery, buttresses, decorative towers and pinnacles, an entrance portal with two doorways and a decorative trim panel above with sculptures and carvings by Lee Lawrie and Ulric Ellerhusen, a 200-foot (62 meter) tall bell tower, at the northeast corner of the building, low aisles with shed roofs on either side of the massive nave, carved wooden interior furnishings and details by Alois Lang, and a cruciform footprint.  The building remains in use as a chapel by the University of Chicago, and in addition to worship services, hosts special events.

The building is clad in limestone with large gothic arched bays housing stained glass windows and tracery, buttresses, decorative towers and pinnacles, an entrance portal with two doorways and a decorative trim panel above with sculptures and carvings by Lee Lawrie and Ulric Ellerhusen, a 200-foot (62 meter) tall bell tower, at the northeast corner of the building, low aisles with shed roofs on either side of the massive nave, carved wooden interior furnishings and details by Alois Lang, and a cruciform footprint.  The building remains in use as a chapel by the University of Chicago, and in addition to worship services, hosts special events.
